metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

brief.text:
The most important thing in today's data is another confirmed attack on a tanker: Adnoc, the UAE state oil company, has confirmed a strike on one of its vessels in UAE territorial waters, described as the latest in a string of hits on the "Hormuz shuttle" route. For anyone fixing ships, that is a direct war-risk and crew-safety question on Arabian Gulf business, and it sits alongside Brent crude at 92.63 dollars a barrel this morning, up 1.14 (+1.2%). Whether the two are connected the data does not establish, though the attack is one plausible factor.

On prices, today's moves are in energy and bunkers. WTI, the US crude benchmark, is 86.77 (+0.8%), gasoil 4.17 dollars a gallon (+0.9%) and gasoline 2.63 (+0.9%). Against that, VLSFO — the low-sulphur fuel oil most ships burn — fell everywhere today: Fujairah 812.00 dollars a tonne (-7.8%), Singapore 816.50 (-5.5%), Rotterdam 703.00 (-4.1%), Houston 733.50 (-2.2%). Crude up while bunkers drop sharply is unusual and the data here does not show why; treat it as a bunker-cost input, not a signal. No freight benchmark has refreshed today. The Baltic Dry Index, which tracks dry bulk charter rates, stood at 2,862 points on Tuesday 10 November, with Panamax at 2,075 and Supramax at 1,806 the same day; the Capesize index (the largest dry bulk ships) was 4,097 on Wednesday 4 November. Tanker earnings are older still: VLCC TD3C, the Gulf-to-China crude run, was 1,303,616 dollars a day on Sunday 8 November — TCE means time charter equivalent, the daily earnings left after voyage costs.

Running stories: the Hormuz attack thread developed today with the Adnoc confirmation. The Russian diesel story also moved — a Greek-owned tanker believed to carry Russian diesel has paused off the US East Coast, with Washington's energy chief saying the cargo will eventually arrive. New today, the US has formally extended its suspension of port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels by two months. Black Sea attacks, shadow-fleet sanctions and chokepoint transits had no fresh headlines today and are unchanged.

Watch two things: whether tanker benchmarks refresh and how they sit after the Adnoc strike, given how stale the current prints are; and the Russian diesel cargo off the US coast, which bears on MR and LR clean product employment.

storylines.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping and energy infrastructure in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November, including crew abandoning a tanker, a US strike on a bulker in the Gulf of Oman, a Houthi hit on Saudi Aramco's headquarters and a strike on the East-West Pipeline. Adnoc has now confirmed a strike on one of its tankers inside UAE territorial waters.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and crew-safety objections raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners, while damaged pipelines can push barrels back onto ships.
storylines.latest: Adnoc confirmed another attack on one of its tankers in UAE waters, described as the latest on the 'Hormuz shuttle' route.
sources: Adnoc Confirms Strike on Tanker in UAE's Territorial Waters

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims carried military goods for Ukraine, plus two electricity substations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022. Russian crude exports on G7 tankers fell in October as Greek operators chose better-paying trades.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and designations force charterers and insurers to re-verify documents and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: Trade press reports Russian crude exports on G7 tankers fell sharply in October as Greek operators steered away from Black Sea conflicts for stronger earnings elsewhere.
sources: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
sources: Adnoc Confirms Strike on Tanker in UAE's Territorial Waters

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January. A Greek-owned tanker believed to carry Russian diesel has paused its voyage off the US East Coast.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
storylines.latest: A tanker linked to the diesel waiver paused off the US East Coast awaiting orders, with the US energy chief saying the cargo would eventually arrive.
sources: Tanker Linked to Trump's Russian Diesel Waiver Pauses off U.S. East Coast
Russian Diesel Tanker Awaits Orders Off U.S. Coast Amid Import Ban Dispute

storylines.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships

storylines.why_it_matters: The fees, if reinstated, would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
storylines.latest: The two-month extension of the suspension was formalised today.

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims carried military goods for Ukraine, plus two electricity substations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022. Russian crude exports on G7 tankers fell in October as Greek operators chose better-paying trades.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and designations force charterers and insurers to re-verify documents and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: Trade press reports Russian crude exports on G7 tankers fell sharply in October as Greek operators steered away from Black Sea conflicts for stronger earnings elsewhere.
sources: Russian crude exports fall on G7 tankers as Greek operators flee for better earnings

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
sources: Adnoc Confirms Strike on Tanker in UAE's Territorial Waters

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January. A Greek-owned tanker believed to carry Russian diesel has paused its voyage off the US East Coast.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
storylines.latest: A tanker linked to the diesel waiver paused off the US East Coast awaiting orders, with the US energy chief saying the cargo would eventually arrive.
sources: Tanker Linked to Trump's Russian Diesel Waiver Pauses off U.S. East Coast
Russian Diesel Tanker Awaits Orders Off U.S. Coast Amid Import Ban Dispute

storylines.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
storylines.what: The US administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
storylines.why_it_matters: The fees, if reinstated, would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
storylines.latest: The two-month extension of the suspension was formalised today.
sources: U.S. Formalizes Two-Month Extension of China Ship Port Fee Suspension
